name: Streif & Hahnenkamm-Stadion
kurzbeschreibung: The Hahnenkamm-Stadion is the finish line of the famous Streif downhill and the venue of the legendary Hahnenkamm-Rennen in the Ski World Cup.
preis: Bergbahn Hahnenkamm Berg- und Talfahrt ca. 31 € (Einzelfahrt ca. 22 €)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Streif downhill on the Hahnenkamm mountain in Kitzbühel is universally acclaimed as the most daring, perilous, and prestigious alpine ski racecourse on the planet. Every January, the legendary Hahnenkamm Races draw the world's finest downhill racers and more than 80,000 spectators to the Tyrolean resort town. Stretching 3,312 meters with an 860-meter vertical drop, elite racers plunge down the mountain reaching top speeds of up to 145 km/h. In summer, this legendary battlefield transforms into an accessible alpine hiking experience: the multimedia "Streif Panorama Trail" descends directly along the original race line from the Start House at 1,665 meters down to the finish area. At four interactive stations—the Start House, the terrifying Mausefalle with an 85% gradient, the Steilhang rock shelf, and the Hausbergkante—visitors discover the jaw-dropping physics and heroic folklore that forged modern ski racing.

Route & Requirements

The excursion begins aboard the iconic red cabins of the Hahnenkammbahn gondola, each emblazoned with the name of a historic downhill victor. Departing the mountain terminal (1,658 m), a brief level stroll reaches the historic Start House. Here, hikers choose between two experiences: families and leisure walkers follow the wide, scenic farm lane past the Seidlalm chalet down to town (easy grade T1). True mountain enthusiasts can hike directly along the race line via the Mausefalle, Steilhang, and Hausberg Traverse into the finish stadium (2 to 2.5 hours downhill walking time, 860 vertical meters descent, moderate grade T2). Because grass slopes in the Mausefalle are precipitous, engineered bypass steps skirt the steepest cliff zones. Rigid ankle-high hiking boots with deep lugged soles and trekking poles are essential for knee support on the descent. At the base, visitors explore the finish stadium and Kitzbühel Ski Club clubhouse. Leashed dogs are permitted on trails and inside gondolas.

Visit & Arrival

Rail transit is exceptionally convenient: regional ÖBB trains stop at the dedicated "Kitzbühel Hahnenkamm" station, situated just a two-minute stroll from the lift terminal. Motorists take the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wörgl-Ost) and follow highway B170 through the Brixental into Kitzbühel. Pay parking is available right beside the base terminal. The Hahnenkamm gondola operates daily from late May through late October between 8:30 AM and 5:00 PM.

Tips

Step onto the viewing platform at the Start House and gaze down the dizzying initial plunge to comprehend the psychological courage required of racers. Pause halfway down at the historic Seidlalm—where the concept of the Alpine Ski World Cup was conceived in 1966—to savor hot plum compote and fluffy pancakes on the scenic meadow terrace overlooking the Wilder Kaiser.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Hahnenkammbahn täglich in Betrieb)
